experiment.probe: create-once unique-intent first-writer deduplication on one dedicated role-local GitHub contents path

scope: One dedicated role-local path using the connected GitHub contents create_file surface. The first create committed intent_id cross-field-r251-unique-intent-1 with effect_counter=1. A second create call to the identical path, deliberately expressing effect_counter=2, was rejected with HTTP 422 because an existing path requires a sha/update route. Exact post-rejection readback returned the identical blob SHA and effect_counter=1.
semantic_conclusion: Within this exact provider-specific single-path sequential scope, create-once path identity acts as a first-writer deduplication primitive: the first create commits one effect and a later create to the identical path cannot silently create a second effect. This complements r249 stale expected-blob rejection and r250 read-before-write same-intent retry suppression. It does not establish behavior for concurrent requests arriving before path visibility, multi-provider durability, actual network partitions, or full Phase-1 parity.
